brief: A 15-second cinematic film of the Golden Gate Bridge at sunrise: open on fog rolling across the bay with the bridge small in the distance, then a low close shot rising up one of the orange towers, then a shot gliding beneath the bridge deck, and end looking out to the open ocean with the title 'Golden Hour'.
checks: Is fog visible drifting across the bay with the Golden Gate Bridge appearing small and distant at the very start of the video?
Is this fog‑bay view the first image shown, with nothing preceding it?
Does the fog visibly move (laterally or vertically) across the frame while the bridge stays at a constant small scale?
Is the camera positioned low, looking up at one bridge tower, and is the tower’s orange paint clearly visible?
Does this tower shot follow directly after the fog‑bay shot, with no other scenes in between?
Does the view rise smoothly along the tower, showing a continuous upward motion?
Is the camera underneath the bridge deck, revealing the steel structure and the water/sky below?
Does this beneath‑deck shot come immediately after the tower‑rise shot, with no intervening shots?
Does the camera glide smoothly forward or laterally beneath the deck, without jerks or sudden stops?
Does the final view look out over the open ocean with the horizon visible, and does the text “Golden Hour” appear on screen?
Is this ocean‑with‑title shot the last segment, appearing after the beneath‑deck shot and lasting until the end?
Does the text appear (fade‑in or slide‑in) and remain legible and stationary while the ocean view holds steady, with no abrupt cuts?
